security_audit.summary: The skill is a Markdown Nmap guide with no bundled executable code, so many backtick and hard-link alerts are formatting false positives. Confirmed risks remain because it instructs agents to use Nmap, sudo/raw packet scans, broad port discovery, vulnerability scripts, and stealth or evasion techniques. Marketplace publication should require clear authorization warnings and execution guardrails.

remediation.issue: Default workflow recommends broad privileged scanning.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit scope confirmation and user approval before any sudo, all-port, UDP, or vulnerability scan command is run.

remediation.issue: Stealth and IDS evasion guidance is included.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evasion-focused language or restrict it to defensive lab contexts with documented authorization.

remediation.issue: Target authorization is mentioned late in the document.
remediation.suggestion: Move authorization, scope, rate limit, and production-impact checks to the first workflow step.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples can be misread as automatic execution steps.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as templates and require the user to supply approved targets before command generation.

static_findings.snippet: **IMPORTANT**: Always save nmap output to an organized directory structure. By default, use `./nmap-
- `-Pn`: Skip host discovery, treat host as online
- `-p <OPEN_PORT_LIST>`: Only scan the ports found to be open (e.g., `-p 23,80,443,554,8000`)
- `-sC`: Run default NSE scripts for additional enumeration
- `-oA`: Output in all formats (normal, XML, grepable)
- `-sS`: SYN stealth scan (doesn't complete TCP handshake)
- `--top-ports 100`: Scan top 100 UDP ports (UDP scanning is slow)
- `-A`: Enable OS detection, version detection, script scanning, traceroute
- `-T4`: Aggressive timing template (faster but more detectable)
- `--script vuln`: Run NSE vulnerability detection scripts
- `-oA`: Output in all formats (normal, XML, grepable)
2. Check for "Host seems down" and retry with `-Pn` if needed
Always use `-oA <prefix>` to generate all three formats:
- `.xml` - XML format for parsing/importing into tools
**Fast scans**: Use `-T4` when speed is important and network can handle it
- Consider using `--source-port 53` or other trusted ports

content.value_statement: Manual network scans can miss ports and produce messy evidence. This skill guides authorized Nmap scans, output organization, and service summaries.
actual_capabilities: Plans two-phase Nmap scans for authorized targets.
Suggests TCP, UDP, service detection, OS detection, and vulnerability scan options.
Organizes scan outputs into repeatable Nmap result files.
Extracts open ports from saved Nmap output for follow-up scans.
Summarizes discovered services, versions, scripts, and notable findings.
limitations: Requires Nmap and required privileges on the local system.
Cannot verify that the user owns or may scan a target.
Network scans can trigger alerts or affect fragile services.
Does not replace professional authorization, scoping, or legal review.

use_cases.description: Plan and document a scoped Nmap scan for a single approved host or subnet.

use_cases.title: Inventory Internal Services
use_cases.description: Identify open ports and service versions on managed internal systems.

use_cases.title: Review IoT Exposure
use_cases.description: Check approved IoT devices for exposed web, RTSP, MQTT, and management services.

prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: define scope before running Nmap.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an authorized Nmap scan for one host. Ask me for target, scope, timing limits, and output location first.

prompt_templates.title: Run Service Enumeration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: enumerate services after open ports are known.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have authorization for this target. Guide me through service detection on these open ports and explain each option before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Saved Results
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: interpret existing Nmap output files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my saved Nmap results, summarize open ports and versions, and identify findings that need manual validation.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Scoped Test Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine TCP, UDP, and focused NSE checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scoped Nmap workflow for an authorized IoT assessment, including safe timing, output naming, and follow-up checks by service type.

output_examples.input: Plan a scan for an approved internal web server.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step scan plan with scope confirmation, output directory, port discovery, service detection, and a final summary checklist.

output_examples.input: Summarize these Nmap results for a managed camera device.
output_examples.output: A concise report listing open ports, detected services, possible device roles, notable scripts, and follow-up validation items.

output_examples.input: Help me choose a scan type for a sensitive production subnet.
output_examples.output: A cautious recommendation that favors limited scope, slower timing, documented approval, and clear stop conditions.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and target scope before any scan.
Save outputs consistently so findings can be reviewed and reproduced.
Use conservative timing on production or fragile networks.
anti_patterns: Scanning public or third-party systems without explicit permission.
Running broad sudo scans before confirming scope and impact limits.

faq.answer: It provides guidance and commands. Execution depends on the agent environment and user approval.

faq.question: Is authorization required?
faq.answer: Yes. You must confirm authorization and target scope before running any scan.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Nmap must be installed. Some scan types also require elevated privileges.

faq.question: Can it scan UDP services?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes UDP scan guidance, but UDP scans are slower and need careful scoping.

faq.question: Can it interpret scan output?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help summarize open ports, service versions, scripts, and follow-up questions.

faq.question: Is it safe for production networks?
faq.answer: Only with approved scope, conservative timing, monitoring awareness, and clear stop conditions.
